body:
In article <19980129022900.VAA07424@ladder02.news.aol.com>,
  esjeje1@aol.com (Esjeje1) wrote:

> According to the promo, at the current rate, the population of the U.S.  will
> be 450 million in the next century. That figure doesn't include the rest of
> North America. I don't think that even the current system can support that,
and
> I have my serious doubts about the quality of life if this ever comes true.
>
> So, something needs to be done. People need to take Ted Kaczynski's ideas
> seriously.
>
> Overpopulation is a long ignored problem. I've read articles and seen TV shows
> about the affects of crowding on lab animals, how they develop abnormal
> behavior. Are people doing the same thing?
>

Esjejel might want to revisit #204:  "Revolutionaries should have as many
children as they can.  There is strong scientific evidence that social
attitudes are to a significant extend inherited... and #205:  The trouble
is that many of the people are who are inclined to rebel against the
industrial system are also concerned about the population problems, hence
they are apt to have few or no children.  In this way they may be
handling the world over to the sort of people who support or at least
accept the industrial system.  To insure the strength of the next
generation of revolutionaries the present generation should reproduce
itself abundantly.  In doing so they will be worsening the population
problem only slightly.	And the important problem is to get rid of the
industrial system, because once the industrial system is gone the world's
population necessarily will decrease (see #167); whereas, if the
industrial system survives, it will continue developing new techniques of
food production that may enable the world's population to keep increasing
almost indefinitely."

One of the many moments in which K's psyche gets the better of him, and
one of the many moments in which he and I part company.
